conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's begin. To determine your Child Benefit eligibility, I first need to understand your situation.

**Do you have a child (or children) you're responsible for?** If yes, please tell me:
- How old is your child (or how old are your children)?
- What are their names? (This will help me keep track if you have multiple children)

The eligibility depends on the child's age, as:
- Children under 16 may automatically qualify
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over generally don't qualify

Please share these details so I can assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have a child I'm responsible for. His name is Alex and he's 11 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex who is 11 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the automatic qualification age category. However, I need to check a few more things to confirm eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is a standard check to ensure that the child isn't working full-time. For an 11-year-old, this is typically not an issue, but I need to confirm this as part of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 11, so he's just in school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's perfect! Alex isn't working, which is what we'd expect for an 11-year-old in school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?** 

In other words, Alex is not receiving benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own name, correct?

Again, for an 11-year-old this would be unusual, but I need to confirm this as part of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 11-year-old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 11 and in regular school, I assume he's not in any kind of apprenticeship program. Can you confirm that?

(Just for context, certain types of apprenticeships can affect eligibility for children aged 16-19, but this wouldn't typically apply to an 11-year-old in regular school.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just in regular school like any other 11-year-old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in regular school, so no apprenticeship concerns.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check about **your residency status** as the claimant.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?** You can qualify if ANY of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**, or
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or
3. You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, job-seeking, studying, or have sufficient resources), or
4. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

The most common situation is simply that you normally live in the UK. **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Birmingham.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live in Birmingham, so you meet the UK residency requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** You qualify if ANY of the following apply:

1. **You live with Alex**, or
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care - things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents), or
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

**Do you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me yet. But I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep for things like clothes and other expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex doesn't live with you, but you do contribute financially towards his upkeep.

To determine if your contributions qualify you as responsible for Alex, I need to understand a bit more:

**Do you contribute at least the equivalent of what Child Benefit would pay towards Alex's care?** 

Currently, Child Benefit is:
- £25.60 per week (about £111 per month) for the eldest or only child
- £16.95 per week (about £73 per month) for additional children

Your contributions can include things like:
- Clothes
- Food
- Pocket money
- Housing costs
- Presents
- Other expenses for his care

These can be weekly, monthly, or even lump sum payments. **Are you contributing at least this amount (around £111 per month or £25.60 per week) towards Alex's upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep, so that's more than the Child Benefit amount. I help with clothes, school things, and other expenses he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're contributing £30 per week, which is more than the Child Benefit amount of £25.60 per week, so you do meet the responsibility requirement for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at any given time. For example:

- Is Alex's other parent (or another person responsible for him) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- If someone else is claiming, have they agreed to transfer the claim to you?
- Or is no one else claiming Child Benefit for Alex at all?

Please let me know the situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, so there's no conflict there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about Alex's living situation.

**Which of the following best describes Alex's current situation?**

1. Alex is in hospital
2. Alex is in care (looked after by the local authority)
3. Alex is fostered
4. Alex is living normally (none of the above apply)

What applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally - none of those special situations apply to him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is living in a normal situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, the local council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or upkeep, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the local council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me now navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Assessment Result for Alex:**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex! Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you qualify because you're contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep, which exceeds the required amount.

### ✅ Why You're Eligible:

- Alex is 11 years old (under 16 - automatically qualifies)
- Alex is not working
- Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- Alex is in regular school (not in a disqualifying apprenticeship)
- You normally live in the UK (Birmingham)
- You're responsible for Alex through your weekly contributions of £30
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is living normally (not in hospital, care, or fostered)
- The local council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### 📝 Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earn over £60,000, you may need to pay some or all of it back through tax
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can find more information and apply here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about the application process or anything else?

All eligibility criteria have been met.
